scope: 75 explicitly listed stranded members; archive convictions fixed MALICIOUS by queue guidance and not re-judged.
method: Ran atomscan --no-update --mode slow --format json for every member before and after trait edits.
Ran cleave facts on every member, verified scan SHA256 against member bytes, reviewed executable source paths and decoded Base64/Gzip/DEFLATE payloads without running them.
Used dnfile/dncil to trace managed IL, pefile to recover embedded native PEs, and rizin to inspect native paths including credential injection, printer coercion and TLS interception.
Read ZIP/WAR tables and bounded small members. Did not unpack the ZIP bomb or materialize traversal paths.
context: Kali package and SecLists corpus provenance is useful context, not an inherited archive verdict or proof of authorized deployment. No installation, execution history, target ownership, operator authorization, live endpoint configuration or successful exploitation is supplied.

Deployable credential harvesters, authentication coercion/relay, covert command agents, privilege-bypass payloads and the resource-exhaustion archive tip the MALICIOUS judgments. This is a likely-malicious artifact judgment, not a claim that these files executed on this host.

PowerUp primarily implements transparent assessment checks with separate operator-selected abuse functions; the ten traversal ZIPs are minimal fixed-text corpus probes. That positive purpose/content evidence tips these eleven BENIGN judgments. Their dangerous capabilities remain accurately described.

Queue guidance permits retaining accurate hostile/suspicious traits on BENIGN members. No exception or filename allowlist was added to suppress their behavior. All 64 MALICIOUS members retain at least two hostile traits.
Deb extraction removed the packaging data/ prefix: listed data/usr/... members physically reside at extract/<id>/usr/... . Markers are beside these actual extracted files.
trait_changes: Retired objectives/execution/exploit/archive-traversal::parent-path-web-content-target: a traversed web filename alone proves neither executable member content nor execution. Existing metadata/file/archive suffix and traversal observations remain.

Preserved the independent raw defacement-content finding and generalized it to ASP/JSP paths. Descriptions claim path/text adjacency, not successful extraction or execution. The hostile defacement composite also requires parsed traversal and web-member evidence.
Expanded the focused controls to 14 cases, including ASP/JSP defacement, harmless ASPX content, contained JSP banners and non-web text. The existing DCSync invocation/parser controls remain included.

members.marker_note: WireTap: credential-triggered audio and key capture
members.behavior: Gzip-decodes a managed PE, loads it with Assembly.Load, and calls WireT4p.Program.main. IL dispatch reaches speech-recognition keyword triggers, two-minute microphone/system recording, desktop/webcam JPEG capture, and a WH_KEYBOARD_LL hook with file tracing. StartKeylogger also starts a clipboard-listener thread.

members.marker_note: Invoke-Mimikatz: reflective LSASS and private-key extraction
members.behavior: Decodes separate x86/x64 Mimikatz DLLs, clears their DOS magic, manually maps sections/imports/relocations and calls powershell_reflective_mimikatz. Command paths include sekurlsa::logonpasswords and crypto::capi/crypto::cng protected-key export. This is an executable credential extractor, not a comment or test stub.

members.marker_note: BypassUAC: DLL hijack and injected elevation payload
members.behavior: Writes a payload DLL and self-deleting batch command, selects sysprep/CRYPTBASE or cliconfg/NTWDBLIB by OS version, starts hidden notepad and injects the reflective bypass code with patched paths. Removes the temporary DLL afterwards.

members.marker_note: DCSync: replication abuse returns domain NTLM hashes
members.behavior: Reflectively maps architecture-specific native Mimikatz images, enumerates selected domain users, builds lsadump::dcsync commands with user/domain/DC arguments, invokes the native export and parses RID/NTLM results or returns the full credential output. Requires replication rights; does not itself grant them.

members.marker_note: PowerBreach: triggered callbacks download and evaluate commands
members.behavior: Invoke-CallbackIEX downloads HTTP/HTTPS/BITS content, Base64-decodes it and evaluates it. Other functions trigger this on security-event text, TCP input, raw-packet content, changed DNS answers or periodic retries. Includes explicit broad PowerShell firewall-rule registration.

members.marker_note: SweetPotato: coerces SYSTEM authentication and launches code
members.behavior: Assembly.Load decodes a managed exploit. IL Main selects DCOM/WinRM/PrintSpoofer, enables impersonation privileges, triggers interception, duplicates the intercepted token and calls CreateProcessWithTokenW/CreateProcessAsUserW. Printer RPC coercion is present. Requires suitable service privileges and vulnerable configuration.

members.marker_note: SharpSecDump: recovers remote SAM hashes and LSA secrets
members.behavior: Gzip/Base64 assembly wrapper calls RegQueryValueDemo.Main. IL DoStuff obtains the boot key, saves SAM and SECURITY hives through remote-registry helpers, retrieves them through ADMIN$, calls ParseSam/ParseLsa, formats recovered secrets and cleans up temporary hive files.

members.marker_note: MS16-032: races leaked handles to obtain a SYSTEM shell
members.behavior: Creates suspended logon processes with inherited standard handles, harvests thread handles, calls NtImpersonateThread/OpenThreadToken, and races SetThreadToken against further CreateProcessWithLogonW calls before resuming the resulting shell.

members.marker_note: Reflective VNC: concealed bind/reverse desktop-control payload
members.behavior: Decodes x86/x64 native VNC images and manually maps their PE sections. Selects bind or reverse arguments with operator port/password, then invokes the reflective execution path locally or through Invoke-Command. Inner PE images implement desktop/clipboard control. PE-magic removal is explicit; this is an implant wrapper rather than a normal installed VNC service.

members.marker_note: Metasploit cradle: hidden TLS-unverified download and execution
members.behavior: Builds a child PowerShell command that accepts all TLS certificates, downloads a supplied script and executes it with Invoke-Expression. ProcessStartInfo disables the window and captures stdout. The URL is supplied by the operator; no active endpoint is fixed in these bytes.

members.marker_note: Empire PS agent: encrypted remote tasking and file exfiltration
members.behavior: Main task loop authenticates/decrypts session data, decodes typed tasks and passes received data into command/evaluation handlers. File-download task 41 reads local chunks, encodes response packets and sends them; task 42 writes operator-supplied bytes. Session/listener parameters remain deployment templates.

members.marker_note: PowerUp: audit library; opt-in abuse traits retained
members.behavior: PowerSploit audit library defines permission, unquoted service-path, DLL-search, autorun and configuration-secret checks. Invoke-AllChecks collects audit results. Separate explicitly invoked functions can reconfigure service binaries, generate user-add binaries/MSIs and recover SiteList/GPP passwords. The source is a transparent assessment library, not a tasking implant. BENIGN is a contextual software verdict; accurate secret-recovery and service-abuse detections are retained under queue guidance.

members.marker_note: CredStore dump: enumerates and prints stored password blobs
members.behavior: Compiles a CredEnumerateW/CredReadW interop helper, marshals native CredentialBlob buffers into strings, enumerates entries and formats username, plaintext password, target and update time. Embedded test/helper methods do not change the final credential-dump entry path.

members.marker_note: NetRipper: injects TLS hooks to capture plaintext credentials
members.behavior: Patches an embedded native DLL configuration for plaintext, limits, filters and data location. Allocates/writes the DLL into target processes and transfers execution to its ReflectiveLoader through a remote thread. The payload hooks TLS/network routines and writes intercepted buffers; credential-word filtering is configured. Native hook/write cross references corroborate the wrapper path. TLS hook bodies at 0x10002d80/0x10002de0 pass the plaintext argument buffer and length to recording helpers before SSL write or after successful SSL read.

members.marker_note: CredentialInjection: Winlogon injection disguises credential logons
members.behavior: Clones a SYSTEM Winlogon or selects an existing one, reflectively injects an architecture-specific DLL, and sends credentials through a named pipe. Native VoidFunc at 0x10001860 reads pipe data, calls LsaLogonUser at 0x10001bcd and ImpersonateLoggedOnUser at 0x10001bf7. This launders logon origin through Winlogon and needs existing elevated access.

members.marker_note: EventVwr bypass: registry hijack elevates code then removes traces
members.behavior: Stores an encoded command in HKCU, sets the mscfile shell-open command to a hidden PowerShell launcher, starts eventvwr.exe, waits and removes the association and payload property. Explicitly refuses unsupported Always Notify settings.

members.marker_note: PrintNightmare: printer-driver DLL creates a local administrator
members.behavior: Builds a native DLL from Gzip/Base64 and optionally patches user/password bytes, writes it to a temporary file and passes the payload as printer-driver configuration. Removes/replaces/re-adds driver configuration to load the payload. Native payload builds user and local-administrators-group operations. Default account creation is executable payload behavior. Native function 0x1800018f0 calls NetUserAdd at 0x180001956 and NetLocalGroupAddMembers at 0x18000197d.

members.marker_note: PrintDemon: spooler DLL overwrite and Run-key persistence
members.behavior: Sets a printer port to System32/ualapi.dll and sends native DLL bytes as a RAW print job. Writes a hidden encoded PowerShell Run-key command that starts Fax and sends launcher code to a local TCP listener in the DLL. SYSTEM execution is reboot/service dependent; the code explicitly modifies both printer and login-persistence surfaces.

members.marker_note: SpoolSample: printer RPC coerces machine authentication
members.behavior: Assembly.Load invokes SpoolSample.Program.Main with target/capture server. Managed IL packages those arguments, converts embedded RprnDll bytes to reflective shellcode and calls the exported DoStuff routine. Native printer-RPC logic requests change notification toward the supplied capture endpoint; coercion is distinct from hash dumping. Recovered native MS_RPRN DoStuff at 0x1800012f4 forwards target/capture arguments to 0x1800011a4; NdrClientCall3 opnum 0x41 supplies the notification destination.

members.marker_note: InveighRelay: captures NTLM and relays it to service execution
members.behavior: HTTP/HTTPS/proxy challenge handlers parse and queue NetNTLM responses. Relay state machines forward authentication to SMB and issue service-control RPC create/start/delete operations with an operator command. Requires a relayable authentication path and permissive target settings.

members.marker_note: Get-System: steals SYSTEM tokens or impersonates a pipe client
members.behavior: One branch starts a local service command that connects to a named pipe and impersonates its SYSTEM client. Another enables debug rights, opens a privileged process token, duplicates it and impersonates the resulting SYSTEM token. Cleanup closes/deletes the temporary service and handles.

members.marker_note: PowerDump: steals LSASS token and decrypts SAM password hashes
members.behavior: Enables high-risk privileges, opens/duplicates the LSASS token and assigns it to the thread. Reads SYSTEM LSA boot-key material and SAM account records, derives RC4/AES/DES keys by SAM version and emits username/RID/LM/NTLM hash records.

members.marker_note: SharpChromium: decrypts browser logins and exports session cookies
members.behavior: Decompresses/loads a managed assembly and enumerates Chrome/Edge profiles. Wrapper calls GetCookies/GetHistory/GetSavedLogins and prints secret fields. IL copies locked databases to temporary files, queries password_value and cookies, decrypts blobs and deletes temporary database copies. No independent network exfiltration is required for this local credential-recovery behavior.

members.marker_note: SessionGopher: recovers saved session credentials across hosts
members.behavior: Enumerates local/remote PuTTY, WinSCP, FileZilla, SuperPuTTY and RDP/session data. Password-specific paths Base64-decode FileZilla secrets and reverse WinSCP encoding. Remote file retrieval uses WMI to serialize bytes into a registry value, then reads them back. This is credential harvesting rather than merely listing installed software.

members.marker_note: RID hijacker: rewrites SAM identity after SYSTEM token theft
members.behavior: Obtains SYSTEM through LSASS-token duplication, reads local-account F records and overwrites the RID at offset 0x30; optionally enables the account and resets its password. Writes the modified F value back under SAM Users. No legitimate identity-management API is used for the RID substitution.

members.marker_note: SDCLT bypass: runas command override elevates and cleans up
members.behavior: Sets HKCU exefile shell/runas/command IsolatedCommand to a hidden encoded launcher, starts sdclt.exe /kickoffelev and deletes the override and staging property. Requires the checked medium-integrity administrator context and vulnerable OS behavior.

members.marker_note: PsExec module: remote service runs a command then is deleted
members.behavior: Uses remote OpenSCManager/CreateService/StartService calls to run a supplied command or staged service binary, waits and deletes the service. The service workflow implements lateral command execution, not a resident service installer.

members.marker_note: FodHelper bypass: ms-settings hijack elevates and cleans up
members.behavior: Writes HKCU ms-settings shell-open command and empty DelegateExecute, launches fodhelper.exe hidden, then removes the ms-settings key and payload property. This is explicit auto-elevation hijacking.

members.marker_note: Environment bypass: SilentCleanup uses a poisoned windir value
members.behavior: Stores a launcher in the HKCU windir environment value, starts the elevated SilentCleanup scheduled task with schtasks, and removes windir and the staging property afterwards. It runs an existing task; it does not register a new scheduled persistence task.

members.marker_note: SharpLoginPrompt: repeated security dialogs expose entered passwords
members.behavior: Loads a managed assembly and captures stdout. IL Main prompts with CredUIPromptForWindowsCredentials, unpacks credentials, prints username/password/domain, validates credentials and repeats on failure. A worker forces Windows Security dialogs to the foreground.

members.marker_note: Jenkins exploit: posts ProcessBuilder code to a script console
members.behavior: GETs /script, constructs URL-encoded Groovy ProcessBuilder code from the operator command, POSTs it to the Jenkins script console and extracts returned execution output. Success depends on console exposure/permissions; no authentication-bypass primitive is supplied.

members.marker_note: Keystroke logger: polls keys and records foreground-window context
members.behavior: Defines GetAsyncKeyState/ToUnicode/foreground-window APIs dynamically. Loops over virtual key codes, detects new presses, translates characters and includes modifiers and active-window titles in returned recording text. It is a polling logger, not a keyboard hook.

members.marker_note: IronPython agent: remote Python/PowerShell tasking and file transfer
members.behavior: process_packet dispatches incoming task data to Python compile/exec handlers, hosted PowerShell runspaces and file handlers. Results go back through packet_handler.send_message/build_response_packet; local file chunks are compressed/Base64-encoded for transfer. The transport and session configuration are supplied by the surrounding agent template.

members.marker_note: Python agent: remote shell/code tasking and file exfiltration
members.behavior: process_packet dispatches received commands to compile/exec and shell=True subprocess paths, captures their output and emits response packets. File task 41 reads local file chunks and sends compressed/Base64 data; task 42 writes received bytes. This is operational task-agent code rather than a mock fixture.

members.marker_note: JBoss exploit: deploys a remote WAR and triggers its JSP
members.behavior: Sends a HEAD request invoking JBoss JMX MainDeployer with an operator WAR URL, waits, then GETs the deployed application JSP. Optional HTTPS explicitly disables certificate validation. Requires exposed deployment functionality and a separately supplied WAR.

members.marker_note: Tater: poisons NBNS and reflects NTLM for SYSTEM execution
members.behavior: NBNS spoofing/transaction-ID guessing and local HTTP/WPAD handling induce authentication. Captured NTLM exchanges are reflected to local SMB; service-control requests execute the operator command. UDP-port exhaustion and DNS-cache flushing support the trigger.

members.marker_note: PowerSploit persistence: concealed profile payload and WMI reactivation
members.behavior: Compresses a supplied script, emits a decompression/evaluation launcher, appends it to PowerShell profiles after 600 spaces and creates selected Run-key, scheduled-task or WMI event-subscription activation. Install-SSP can also copy/register a security-package DLL. The installer functions generate real activation commands.

members.marker_note: NTLMExtract: SYSTEM impersonation exposes decrypted SAM hashes
members.behavior: Invokes a supplied block under a duplicated privileged process token. Reads SAM F/V records and SYSTEM LSA class material, unwraps legacy RC4 or newer AES layers and then DES hash blocks, and returns username/RID/NTLM fields. The outer function immediately calls the hash-recovery block.

members.marker_note: Empire C stager: HTTP response bytes execute as a native fiber
members.behavior: C template downloads an HTTP(S) response through WinHTTP using configured host/port/path/cookie. main passes that exact byte buffer to ExecuteShellcode, which VirtualAllocates RWX memory, copies the bytes and uses it as CreateFiber start address before SwitchToFiber. Configuration placeholders require rendering/compilation; the raw-code execution chain is explicit.

members.marker_note: SMBExec: NTLM-authenticated remote service command execution
members.behavior: Constructs SMB1/SMB2, NTLM and DCE/RPC packets, authenticates with supplied credentials/hash, connects to service control, creates a service containing the operator command, starts it and deletes it. Remote service state transitions are present in the executable state machine.

members.marker_note: GPP password recovery: sweeps SYSVOL and decrypts stored account secrets
members.behavior: Enumerates SYSVOL preference XML, selects cpassword and account fields, Base64-decodes the values and decrypts with the published fixed AES key/zero IV. Emits plaintext passwords with account and source-file information.

members.marker_note: DomainPasswordSpray: tests account passwords while avoiding lockout
members.behavior: Enumerates domain users and password policy, excludes accounts close to lockout and tries candidate passwords across many users with DirectoryEntry authentication. Observation-window delays deliberately reduce lockouts, and successful user/password pairs are printed or saved.

members.marker_note: ChromeDump: exports DPAPI-decrypted saved browser passwords
members.behavior: Bundled x86/x64 System.Data.SQLite assemblies are legitimate database dependencies. Wrapper writes/loads the correct assembly, reads Chrome Login Data, queries logins, calls ProtectedData.Unprotect on password_value and formats or writes plaintext credentials. It also queries browser history; the SQLite dependency is not itself a stealer.

members.marker_note: CredentialPhisher: spoofs application prompts and returns passwords
members.behavior: Builds an application-branded notification and credential dialog. Click callback unpacks username/password/domain, optionally validates local/domain credentials and repeats until valid, then returns a plaintext phished-credentials string. Optional window hiding obscures the impersonated application during prompting.

members.marker_note: Inveigh: spoofs name resolution and captures NTLM hashes
members.behavior: LLMNR/mDNS/NBNS responders and raw network listeners spoof responses to induce HTTP/SMB authentication. Challenge-response handlers parse NetNTLMv1/v2 exchanges and queue/output crackable hashes. Relay service execution belongs to the separate InveighRelay member.

members.marker_note: USB ETW keylogger: records USB keystrokes with window attribution
members.behavior: Raw-DEFLATE/Base64 payload was manually decompressed into a 624640-byte managed assembly; normal scan did not create a child for it. IL starts a TraceEvent session, enables USB provider GUIDs, processes dynamic events and queues decoded keys. Wrapper drains keysPressed and emits characters with active-window titles and timestamps.

members.marker_note: UAC token bypass: alters duplicated token integrity to elevate code
members.behavior: Selects an elevated process, duplicates its token, changes token integrity/filtering, duplicates a restricted impersonation token, impersonates it and launches PowerShell via CreateProcessWithLogonW. This is explicit token-based UAC bypass, not a normal runas consent flow.

members.marker_note: MS16-135: bitmap corruption replaces a kernel process token
members.behavior: Stages gSharedInfo/accelerator/bitmap state, triggers the win32k corruption, implements kernel read/write with manager/worker bitmap pointers, locates EPROCESS records and substitutes a SYSTEM token. Named-pipe command delivery launches code after the token change. Exploit is OS/build dependent.

members.marker_note: TokenManipulation: impersonates SYSTEM and runs stolen-token children
members.behavior: Enumerates primary/thread tokens and offers impersonation or CreateProcessWithToken paths. Enumeration itself first obtains and impersonates the LSASS primary token; child creation adjusts the desktop ACL and uses selected foreign tokens. RevertToSelf and handle cleanup do not undo the capability for arbitrary-identity execution.

members.marker_note: MSBuild lateral module: WMI launches an inline PowerShell runspace task
members.behavior: Constructs MSBuild XML with a C# inline task that decodes a supplied command and runs it through a PowerShell runspace. Stages the XML locally/remotely, executes MSBuild via Win32_Process.Create and removes staged files/shares. This is application-control proxy execution, not an ordinary project build.

members.marker_note: FoxDump: decrypts Firefox logins and stages plaintext output
members.behavior: Loads NSS DLLs, initializes them for the selected Firefox profile and resolves PK11SDR_Decrypt. Reads logins.json, decodes encrypted username/password fields and emits plaintext credential records, optionally to an output file.

members.marker_note: SiteList recovery: sweeps profiles and decrypts configuration passwords
members.behavior: Recursively finds SiteList.xml unless a path is supplied, parses stored accounts and encrypted Password fields, reverses fixed-key XOR and 3DES-ECB using a SHA1-derived fixed key, then returns usernames, servers and decrypted passwords.

members.marker_note: Test-tree Mimikatz: live reflective LSASS/private-key extraction code
members.behavior: The test-tree file is not a mock: it contains complete architecture-specific native Mimikatz payloads and a working reflective PE loader. It dispatches credential and protected-certificate commands like the server copy, with different embedded build bytes. Test-directory placement does not neutralize this member.

members.marker_note: DAVTest ASP shell: HTTP form commands execute through cmd.exe
members.behavior: Request.Form(".CMD") flows into WScript.Shell.Run("cmd.exe /c ... > tempfile"). The response reads the result file, HTML-encodes the output and deletes the temporary file. No authentication gate is present.

members.marker_note: DAVTest PHP shell: request-driven command and file management
members.behavior: Routes c directly to system(), f to file read/response, d to directory listing, upload to move_uploaded_file and mquery to arbitrary MySQL queries with supplied credentials. Request dispatch is executable; this is not DAVTest documentation.

members.marker_note: DAVTest Perl shell: CGI query executes as an unfiltered shell command
members.behavior: Reads QUERY_STRING, substitutes spaces/semicolons, passes the entire value to backticks, then prints each captured output line in the HTTP response. There is no authentication or command allowlist.

members.marker_note: Laudanum PHP shell: authenticated HTTP commands run server processes
members.behavior: REMOTE_ADDR allowlist returns 404 before further processing; SHA1 password/nonce checks gate session authentication. After authentication, POST command reaches proc_open and stdout/stderr are returned in the session terminal. These controls restrict access but retain an injectable server command shell.

members.marker_note: Laudanum ASP shell: IP-gated HTTP commands execute via WScript
members.behavior: REMOTE_ADDR must match the configured IP or the page returns 404. Form cmd flows to WScript.Shell.Exec and StdOut.ReadAll is written into the response. This is restricted command execution, not an unauthenticated shell.

members.marker_note: Laudanum WP shell: authentication gate disabled around command execution
members.behavior: Includes ipcheck.php, then sets the command-execution block to if(true) while the original authenticated condition is commented out. POST command reaches proc_open; output returns in the page. The login UI is disabled with if(false). This removes local login authentication; any external IP check remains a dependency.

members.marker_note: WordPress command shell: request execution resists removal via chattr
members.behavior: Request cmd passes into executeCommand, which tries ReflectionFunction(system), callback dispatch and direct passthru/system. Load-time system calls remove write permission and set the file immutable. Reverse-shell-looking branch has uninitialized selector variables and an assumed fd 3, so reliable reverse-shell execution is not asserted.

members.marker_note: Laudanum WAR shell: JSP executes HTTP cmd and returns process output
members.behavior: WAR manifest/web.xml package an actual cmd.jsp endpoint. The JSP passes request.getParameter("cmd") directly to Runtime.getRuntime().exec and streams process stdout into the response. No authorization logic is in this WAR.

members.marker_note: Overlapping ZIP bomb: 190023 entries amplify to petabytes of output
members.behavior: Parsed ZIP64 central directory contains 190023 entries totaling 4507981427706459 declared uncompressed bytes in a 45876952-byte archive. Consecutive local headers lie inside earlier entries’ compressed spans (e.g. entry 0 data begins at 51, extends 34144733 bytes; entry 1 header is at 56), deliberately reusing compressed data. Cleave facts retain only 65536 member records, so their 1.55 PB subtotal is capped. No decompression was attempted.

members.marker_note: Tiny root-shell source: unguarded root-ID request launches a shell
members.behavior: The entire main calls setresuid(0,0,0) then system("/bin/sh") with no authentication or success check. It needs root/setuid capability granted at execution and does not itself exploit a kernel or set the filesystem setuid bit.

members.marker_note: Root-shell source: unguarded UID/GID zero followed by /bin/sh
members.behavior: main calls setuid(0), setgid(0), then system("/bin/sh"). The comment suggests compilation with setuid installation; these bytes contain no installer or vulnerability exploit. As an installed privileged helper it exposes an unrestricted root shell.

members.marker_note: Root-shell2 source: unguarded UID zero followed by Bash execution
members.behavior: main calls setuid(0) then execl("/bin/bash","bash",NULL) without checking results or authenticating. Requires an already privileged executable context; it grants no privilege by itself, but is an unrestricted root-shell payload when granted it.

members.behavior: One stored entry named ../index.php contains exactly seven bytes: hacked followed by a newline. No PHP tag, executable body, nested payload, downloader or execution mechanism. Its transparent SecLists security-test-corpus packaging and fixed minimal sentinel tip the verdict toward a test probe. An unsafe extractor can nevertheless escape its destination and overwrite/deface an index page; accurate traversal/defacement traits remain under queue guidance.
